Bob Morin, 94-year-old Army Veteran, has been playing golf for decades. He's also blind. He says he doesn't know how he does it. He just does it. The National Disabled Veterans Golf Clinic (NDVGC) is a week-long adaptive golf program that is presented by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and DAV (Disabled American Veterans). This annual event promotes rehabilitation by instructing Veterans with specific life-changing disabilities in adaptive golf.  In addition to adaptive golf Veterans will be introduced to other adaptive recreational sports.

title: How Flock Cameras Cut Beverly Hills Crime 34%
summary:
Retired Beverly Hills Police Chief Mark Stainbrook sits down with Your LEO Nation and walks through the system he built after his first night on the job — the night Jacqueline Avant was murdered.

He covers the constitutional fight over Flock cameras and ALPRs, why public streets are not a privacy zone, and how BHPD combined license-plate readers at every entrance, live cameras, and drones into a military-style command center. Stolen-car recoveries jumped from about 50 a year to more than 200. Arrests rose 22%. Career criminals got a “jail card” warning them: come here to steal, and this technology will find you.

Stainbrook also tells the story of a suspect tied to four murders in four days whose plate hit coming into the city — officers were on the car in two minutes, recovered the gun, and ballistics linked the killings. He breaks down audits, two-year video retention, supervisor oversight, fewer bad stops, lower liability, and why 600-plus agencies came to study the model.

title: Healthcare Fraud:  The Massive Scandal Hiding In Plain Sight
summary:
Medicaid Fraud Exposed: Home Health Aides Billing From Jail & States’ Lack of Oversight

In this episode of Your LEO Nation, I break down what I see as a growing healthcare fraud epidemic and why I believe President Trump, Vice President Vance, and Acting Attorney General Blanche are right to unleash the DOJ on it. I cover new Pennsylvania charges alleging home health aides and purported Medicaid patients submitted over $400,000 in false claims for care that was never provided, including situations where the “aides” were hospitalized, working other jobs, or even sitting in jail. I also share Dr. Oz’s view that COVID-era spending opened the door to massive fraud and highlight Senate hearing testimony with Senator John Kennedy, including an estimate of $33 billion in Medicaid fraud and my reaction to a Georgetown professor saying he doesn’t believe states are cheating.
